  "explanation": "The dichotomy in §3 is indeed non-exhaustive: V={c} (i.e. f(x)=x+c, the actual answer) fits neither branch (i) nor (ii); this omission is harmless since §6–7 land exactly there, but the second half of the objection is decisive. The write-up never proves g(x) >= 0. The only related line, 'Then g(x) > -x', is far weaker, and §3 only rules out two distinct positive values, silently assuming V contains no negative number before restricting to V ⊆ {0,c}. The standard one-line repair (iterate (4): f^n(x) = x + n g(x) > 0 for all n, so g(x) >= 0) is absent, so L5.3 is not established as written."
